paragraphs: Clouds are gathering over **Pelargir**.

Yet these are not merely the heavy clouds that come out of the east and veil the stars above the broad flow of the Anduin. A darker shadow creeps across the land. The tidings brought by messengers grow worse with every day, and from roads that were safe not long ago only a few now return.

After the fighting in **South Ithilien** and in the marshes there, the forces of the Dark Lord broke the resistance of the defenders and pressed on westward. What at first seemed no more than a run of sorties, probing attacks and raids slowly turned into unrelenting pressure. The companies of Mordor drove ever deeper into the lands of Gondor, and their vanguard appeared at last in the country around Pelargir.
Thus the ancient city upon the Anduin came into peril.
Yet no single mighty blow has fallen to decide its fate. Instead, the whole wide country about the city has become a restless land, where none may be certain to whom the next morning will belong.

In the woods the scouts clash. On the roads ambushes lie in wait. On the stony hillsides patrols of both sides appear, and each strives to catch sight of the enemy before it is itself seen. Sometimes the fight lasts but a few moments: the hiss of arrows among the trees, a short cry, and the retreat of one side back into the forest. At other times a lesser skirmish flares into a fierce encounter, and the clash of arms is heard from afar long after the sun has vanished behind the hills.
But the war is not waged upon land alone. The **Anduin** too has become a battlefield.

Down its current move the ships that supply the city, the boats of scouts and armed vessels whose crews watch both banks closely. In the mist above the water the dark silhouette of a strange ship sometimes appears, and at once the alarm is raised. Arrows fly above the surface, boats strive to slip away with the current, and men fight upon the decks while beneath them the murky water of the Great River runs on towards the sea.
Some ships return to Pelargir damaged and with thinned crews. Others do not return at all.
Yet neither side may withdraw. The coming clash will not be decided by sword and spear alone. As weighty now as the number of warriors are the **supplies**.

Both sides therefore send ever more companies into the country around the city. Food, timber, cloth, iron, rope and all else that may aid the main hosts in the deciding hour must be gathered in. Every wagon of grain, every crate of tools and every bundle of wood may be worth the lives of many men.
The forces of the Dark Lord seek out all that might strengthen the armies mustering before the city. Gondor strives to win the same for the defenders behind the walls.

And so even places that lately held no worth in war become the aim of bloody encounters. A deserted farmstead, a storehouse by the river, a wagon stuck upon the road or a store of wood laid by for winter may change hands several times in a single day.
In this struggle the forces of the Dark Lord held the upper hand for a time.

Their raiding companies spread far and wide around Pelargir and set about plundering its country in earnest. Villages were stripped of their stores, storehouses emptied, and all that might serve the war was carried off to the host mustering before the city. Smoke rose above the land, and along the roads went wagons laden with plunder.
The scouts of Gondor sought to halt them whenever the chance came, but the enemy was numerous, swift and scattered in many places.
At last, however, came an encounter in which the scouting companies of both sides met in open battle. This time the men of Gondor had the upper hand.

After a fierce clash the companies of the Dark Lord were beaten, and their survivors withdrew from the field. For the defenders of Pelargir it was a victory, the first after a long train of ill tidings, and many hoped that at least a part of the enemy's preparations had been undone.
Yet that hope was to last only a little while. For the beaten companies had already fulfilled their chief task.
**The gathered supplies had been brought to the besieging army before ever the final clash was fought.**
What was torn from the surrounding land will now serve against its own defenders.
And before Pelargir an assault is being made ready.

The captains of the Dark Lord know well that a city guarded by walls and by the river will be no easy prey. An assault from the land alone may not suffice. If Pelargir is to fall, the enemy must strike **from land and from water alike**.
Therefore in the camps of the **Corsairs of Umbar** the work does not cease even after sunset.

By day and by night ring the blows of axes and hammers. Hewn beams are stacked upon the banks, ropes are drawn taut, and new ships are built. The Corsairs make ready vessels able to carry warriors and the gear of war, and they seek a way to overcome the defence that still guards the approach to the city from the Anduin.
Up the river come further supplies. Along the banks the fires grow more numerous. And with every day it becomes plainer that the enemy prepares no mere raid. He prepares a **siege**.
Nor are **Gondor and its allies** idle.

Word of the building of the enemy's ships has already passed behind the walls, and the defenders know what is coming. Every material saved in the country about the city is at once turned to the making ready of the defence.

The damaged parts of the fortifications are repaired. The gates are made fast. Stores of missiles, stone and timber are carried up onto the walls. At places of importance new obstacles are raised, and the watches are strengthened.
On the riverbank the wardens watch the current of the Anduin. Upon the walls others look to the east.
Every ship seen in the distance may bring aid — or the enemy. Every cloud of dust upon the road may mean the coming of allies — or another host of Mordor.
And though Pelargir still stands, none doubts any longer that the hardest days are yet to come.
The enemy has supplies. The Corsairs build their ships. The hosts muster before the walls. Gondor fortifies the city and summons all who are able to bear arms.
Darkness falls over the Anduin, and on both banks of the river the fires burn far into the night.
**The Battle of Pelargir draws near.**
